slots.name: Christy Hoffman
slots.bio: Goalkeeper Christy Hoffman helped Cincinnati reach the 2001 NCAA Sweet Sixteen and earned Conference USA Defender of the Year honors. She joined UC's Hall of Fame Class of 2026.

slots.name: Al Lanier
slots.bio: One of UC's track and field all-time greats who garnered a total of five All-American awards. First Bearcat track athlete to qualify for the NCAA Championships in all four seasons, competing in both the long jump and triple jump at the outdoor championships. Earned All-American honors as a junior with a third place finish in the triple jump. Capped his career by capturing All-American plaudits in both the long jump (second place) and triple jump (sixth) as a senior. Also qualified for the NCAA Indoor Championships in the long jump and triple jump his junior and senior campaigns, garnering All-American honors each year in the triple jump. Closed his career holding UC records in both the long jump (26'1 1/2") and triple jump (55'6 1/2"). Narrowly missed earning a berth on the U.S. Olympic Team at the 1972 Trials. Competed on the U.S. Army team that made a tour of China in 1975. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1988.

slots.name: Paulette Angilecchia
slots.bio: Starred at UC from 1993-1996. Three-time All-Conference USA selection. Ranks 3rd in both points(118) and goals(50) and 6th in assists(18) in a season at UC. Twice named to the Conference USA Commissioner's Honor Roll.

slots.name: Phil Meyers
slots.bio: Four-season letterwinner in football. Three-time All-Ohio selection as the right end. Later selected by a panel of sportswriters to UC's All-Time Football Team. Active on campus as a member of the Sigma Sigma honorary and the Sigma Alpha Mue Fraternity. Served on the UC Board of Trustees in the 1950s. Successful builder and developer in the Cincinnati area who was well-known for his philanthropic work. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1977.

slots.name: Dr. Richard Bryant
slots.bio: All-around student-athlete and campus leader. Lettered in football, basketball and track. Served as senior class president, student government vice president, was active in fraternities and social organizations and earned election to Phi Beta Kappa, Cincinnatus Society and Sigma Sigma. Completed his medical degree and served on the staffs of area hospitals while a member of UC's College of Medicine staff. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1984.

slots.name: Annette Echikunwoke
slots.bio: One of Cincinnati’s most decorated track and field athletes. Echikunwoke won the 2017 NCAA Indoor national title in the weight throw, finished runner-up in 2018 and remained the school record holder in four of the five throwing events she contested at UC. She was a seven-time AAC champion, four-time First Team All-American and won the 2024 Olympic silver medal in the hammer throw.

slots.name: Jessie Nevitt
slots.bio: Volleyball standout for Cincinnati from 2005 to 2008. Nevitt was a three-time AVCA Honorable Mention All-American, four-time First Team All-BIG EAST selection and the 2005 BIG EAST Rookie of the Year. She helped UC win its first BIG EAST regular-season title, reach four NCAA Tournaments and finished with 1,498 kills and 652 blocks while ranking in UC’s top 10 in eight statistical categories.

slots.name: Bill Walker, AT
slots.bio: Sports medicine leader who oversaw health care for Cincinnati student-athletes for nearly 32 years. Walker served as UC’s head athletic trainer from December 1975 through July 2007 and was promoted to Assistant AD in 1998. His GoBearcats profile credits him with the growth and expansion of the athletic training department and notes his service as past president of the Greater Cincinnati Athletic Trainers Association.

slots.name: Roger McClendon
slots.bio: Considered UC's player of the decade for the 1980s. Four-year starter who led the team in scoring in each of his first three campaigns. Closed his career as UC's No. 2 career scorer with 1,789 points. Two-time first team All-Metro Conference selection. Team MVP as a junior. Co-captain as a senior. As devoted to academics as he was basketball, completed his degree in engineering. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1998.

slots.name: Elbie Nickel
slots.bio: One of UC's top players of the 1940s and the prototype of a productive tight end. Played on the 1940-41-42 UC teams before entering the service for World War II. Returned to UC following the war to complete his academic and athletic career. Captain of the 1946 team that upset defending Big Ten champion Indiana, a game in which he scored a touchdown and kicked a field goal. Helped UC to a 9-2 record in 1946, capped with an 18-6 win over Virginia Tech in the Sun Bowl, UC's first bowl appearance. Also lettered in basketball and baseball. Played 11 seasons in the NFL with the Pittsburgh Steelers, later earning a selection to the all-time Steelers team at tight end. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1982.

slots.name: Jim Kelly Jr.
slots.bio: Jim Kelly Jr. played wide receiver for Cincinnati from 1972 to 1975, leading the Bearcats in receiving each season from 1973 to 1975 and finishing with 76 catches for 964 yards. After an injury ended his free-agent stint with the Chicago Bears, he returned to UC as a graduate assistant coach and later spent 35 years as the color analyst on Cincinnati football's radio broadcasts. The son of Jim Kelly Sr., the Hall of Fame's namesake, he was inducted as a contributor in 2017. He died in October 2025.

slots.name: Tony Trabert
slots.bio: NCAA Singles Champion 1951, runner-up in doubles (partner Bob Molt). Starting guard on the 1951 Bearcat basketball team that participated in the National Invitation Tournament). Member of the United States Davis Cup teams, 1951-55. Compiled a 26-8 Davis Cup record. Captain of five U.S. Davis Cup teams (1953, 1976-80). No. 1 singles player on the 1954 Davis Cup team that won the cup back from the Australians. U.S. Championships (later known as the U.S. Open) singles champion twice (1953, 1955). U.S. Championships doubles champion (1954). Wimbledon singles champion (1955). Wimbledon doubles runner-up (1954). French Open singles champion twice (1954, 1955). French Open doubles champion (1950; partner Bill Talbert), (1954, 1955; partner Vic Seixas). Italian Open doubles champion (1950; partner Bill Talbert), runner-up (1954). Italian Open mixed doubles champion (1954). Australian Open doubles champion (1955; partner Vic Seixas). Sigma Sigma and ULEX member at UC. Ranked USLTA Singles top 10 four times, reaching No. 1 in 1953 and 1955. National Indoor Junior singles and doubles champion (1948). National Clay Court singles champion twice (1951, 1955). National Clay Court doubles champion three times (1951, 1954, 1955). United States Hardcourt singles champion (1954); doubles champion (1950, 1953). National Indoor singles and doubles champion (1955). World Pro doubles champion (1956). World Pro Singles runner-up (1960). William Howard Taft Medal for Notable Achievement from the UC alumni (1994). Named to the Hamilton County Hall of Fame (1968), the National Lawn Tennis Hall of Fame (1970), the College Tennis Hall of Fame (1983), and the Cincinnati Tennis Hall of Fame (2002). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1977.

slots.name: Kara Molony
slots.bio: Cincinnati women’s tennis standout from 1997 to 2001. Molony became UC’s first women’s tennis player to qualify for the NCAA Championship in 2000, was a three-time All-Conference USA selection and the 2000 C-USA Co-Player of the Year. Her GoBearcats profile lists UC single-season and career singles victory records and notes national rankings as high as No. 22 in singles and No. 27 in doubles with her sister Lyndsey.

slots.name: Mike Whiting
slots.bio: Four-year starter and all-time leading scorer in soccer. Established UC single game records for goals (4), assists (4) and points (10) which stand today. Is UC's career leader in points (115) and assists (31) and is second in goals (42). Earned All-Ohio honors in each of his four seasons. Named to the All-Mideast Team his junior and senior campaigns. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1990.

slots.name: Matt Singer
slots.bio: Baseball outfielder and three-time First Team All-Conference USA selection. GoBearcats’ UC Baseball All-Decade profile says Singer rewrote the record book, combining for a .342 average, 39 doubles, 21 home runs and 119 RBI in 2000 and 2001. He was the 2001 C-USA Scholar-Athlete of the Year and ranked first in five UC offensive career categories, including hits, doubles, RBI, total bases and at-bats.

slots.name: Eddie Coons
slots.bio: Lettered in four sports--football, basketball, baseball and track. Earned All-Ohio honors in both football and basketball. Served as team captain of the basketball and baseball teams as a senior. Outstanding baseball prospect who declined a number of professional offers to enter business with Cincinnati Bell. Returned to UC to serve as Athletics Ticket Manager. Member of the UC Athletic Hall of Fame charter class of inductees.

slots.name: Tom Blake
slots.bio: Stalwart offensive lineman on the successful UC teams of the late 1940s. After playing as a freshman at Tennessee during World War II, he joined the UC varsity in 1946 and became the starting left tackle on the team that posted a 9-2 record and defeated Virginia Tech in the Sun Bowl. Switched to right tackle for his final two seasons and earned a reputation for his hard-nosed play. Team captain as a senior. Inducted into the Sigma Sigma honorary. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1998.

slots.name: Tom O'Malley
slots.bio: Four-year letterman, three-year starter. Ranked among the nation's top 10 leading passers as a junior in 1948. Led the nation in passing yardage (1,617) in 1949, passing for 16 touchdowns. Inserted into the game vs. Miami University as a freshman and fired a touchdown pass that clinched the 13-7 victory and sent UC to the Sun Bowl, its first bowl appearance. Jersey number 27 retired when he concluded his career. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 2006.

slots.name: Trent Cole
slots.bio: Defensive lineman for Cincinnati from 2002 to 2004. Cole was a CollegeFootballNews.com Third Team All-American in 2004, a two-time First Team All-Conference USA selection and UC’s Claude Rost Most Valuable Player and John Pease Outstanding Lineman as a senior. He finished among UC’s all-time leaders in tackles for loss and sacks before a long NFL career.

slots.name: Madinah Slaise
slots.bio: Four-year women’s basketball letterwinner from 1997 to 2000 and one of the top scorers in program history. Slaise ranked third on UC’s career scoring list in the archived GoBearcats profile with 1,849 points and averaged 21.8 points per game as a senior. She was a two-time First Team All-Conference USA selection, made the 1997 C-USA All-Freshman Team and the 1999 C-USA All-Tournament Team, and was selected by the Detroit Shock in the WNBA Draft.

slots.name: Robert Miller
slots.bio: Four-year regular who helped lead UC to three NCAA Tournament appearances, two Metro Conference championships and a 90-27 record. An 8.9-point scorer as a freshman, he scored at a 17.3-point clip in the NCAA Tournament to earn Midwest Regional all-tournament honors. Garnered Bearcat MVP honors his sophomore and junior seasons, during which he was the squad's scoring and rebounding leader. Second-leading scorer and top rebounder and shot blocker as a senior. Became the fourth Bearcat to top the 1,000 plateau in both points (1,498) and rebounds (1,060). Second team All-Metro Conference pick his junior and senior years. Honorable mention All-American as a senior in 1978 (AP). Taken in the fourth round by Phoenix in the 1978 NBA draft to begin a six-season NBA career. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1999.

slots.name: Gene Rossi
slots.bio: Three-year starter and team passing leader. Topped the 1,000-yard mark in passing in each of his three seasons. Concluded his career as UC's all-time leader in passes attempted (492), completions (257), completion percentage (.522), passing yards (4,003) and TD passes (37), all of which still rank him among the Bearcat leaders. Led UC to a 26-6-1 record as a starter. Three-time All-Mid-American Conference selection. Earned All-Ohio honors his junior and senior seasons. Honorable mention All-American in both 1951 (Colliers) and 1952 (AP, UPI, Colliers). Jersey number (28) retired. Selected by Baltimore in the 1953 NFL draft but played professionally in Canada. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1984.

slots.name: Ralph Davis
slots.bio: Three-year starter for the UC teams of the late 1950s that compiled a 79-9 record, won three Missouri Valley Conference titles and made two appearances in the NCAA Final Four, finishing third each time. Co-captain as a senior. High-scoring performer whose talents were overshadowed by Oscar Robertson. Second on the team in scoring and assists his final two seasons, averaging 15.5 points per game as a junior. Was No. 6 on the UC career scoring list when he closed his career with 1,093 points. Earned second team All-American honors as a senior in 1960 (Converse). Taken in the third round of the 1960 NBA draft by Cincinnati. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1981.

slots.name: Wayne Mason
slots.bio: All-American hurdler Wayne Mason competed for Cincinnati from 1977 to 1980 and joined UC's Hall of Fame Class of 2026.

slots.name: Sean Kilpatrick
slots.bio: Men’s basketball guard who scored 2,145 points from 2009 to 2014, second in school history behind Oscar Robertson. Kilpatrick helped Cincinnati win 101 games, reach four NCAA Tournaments and make the 2012 Sweet 16. He earned Associated Press First Team All-America honors in 2013-14, tied the school record for career three-pointers and set program marks for games played, consecutive games played and minutes played.

slots.name: Stephanie Niemer
slots.bio: One of the top players in Cincinnati volleyball history. Niemer was the 2010 BIG EAST Player of the Year, a four-time all-league selection and a two-time AVCA All-America honoree, earning second-team recognition in 2010 and honorable mention in 2009. She finished her UC career ranked first in service aces and second in kills and kills per set before training with the U.S. National Team and playing professionally overseas.

slots.name: Jason Fabini
slots.bio: Three-time first team All-Conference USA selection. Team co-captain. Lettered al four years at UC. Played in 44 games throughout his career making 43 starts. Rated as the 20th best senior in the country in 1997 by NFL Draft expert Mel Kiper. 1996 recipient of the John Pease Award as the team's top offensive lineman.

slots.name: Steve Collier
slots.bio: Mr. Basketball for the state of Indiana as a high school senior lived up to all expectations beginning with his freshman season. Was named team captain as a freshman and helped lead the team to a 23-6 record and a regional finish in the NCAA Tournament. Showed his versatility, surrendering the point guard responsibilities his sophomore and junior campaigns to junior college newcomer Gary Yoder. Played in 114 games, making 104 starts. Member of UC's 1,000-point scorers club (1,252). Earned honorable mention All-Metro Conference honors his junior and senior seasons. Was an honorable mention All-American in 1976 (Street & Smith's). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2000.

slots.name: Nick Skorich
slots.bio: Three-year letterman in football as a rugged two-way lineman. Team captain as a senior. Earned All-Ohio honors and honorable mention All-American mention as a senior. Played three seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Launched his coaching career in the NFL with Pittsburgh and served at Green Bay; was offensive coordinator for the 1961 NFL champion Philadelphia Eagles and defensive coordinator for the 1964 NFL champion Cleveland Browns. Served as head coach of the Philadelphia Eagles (three years) and Cleveland Browns (four years). Was Assistant Supervisor of Officials for the NFL. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1977.

slots.name: Ron Bonham
slots.bio: Starter throughout his three-year varsity career, helping UC compile a record of 72-13 during that period. Helped lead UC to the NCAA National Championship as a sophomore in 1962 and a runner-up finish in 1963. Leading scorer his junior and senior seasons, posting averages of 21.0 and 24.4. Closed his career as UC's second-leading scorer of all-time with 1,666 points, a total which currently ranks him in the top 10. His 19.6-point career scoring average is the third-best in UC history. Three-time All-Missouri Valley Conference selection. Team captain as a senior. Consensus first team All-American in 1963 (AP, UPI, Basketball Writers, Helms, Converse, NABC), third team pick (NEA); earned second team All-American honors in 1964 (AP, UPI, Converse) and was third team (NABC). Columbus Touchdown Club Player of the Year selection in 1963. Taken in the second round by Boston in the 1964 NBA Draft and played on two NBA championship teams for the Celtics. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1986.

slots.name: Chris Wineberg
slots.bio: Men’s track and field standout from 2001 to 2004 and a two-time Conference USA decathlon champion. Wineberg earned USTFCCCA All-America honors in the decathlon in 2004 and held the school record in the event for 17 years. He later served as a UC assistant coach for 17 years, producing 21 NCAA All-Americans, 25 national qualifiers and 26 conference athletes of the meet.

slots.name: Ray Nolting
slots.bio: Three-year starter at halfback in football. Three-time All-Buckeye Athletic Association selection. Earned All-Ohio honors in both his junior and senior seasons. Helped UC compile a 20-6-1 record and win two conference titles during his three seasons. Honorable mention All-American in 1935. Drafted by Chicago and played eight seasons in the NFL. Returned to serve as head coach at UC, 1946-48, directing the Bearcats to their first bowl appearance and a 23-15-1 ledger. Member of the UC Athletic Hall of Fame charter class of inductees.

slots.name: Sonja Jackson
slots.bio: Three time team Most Valuable Player. Earned first team All-Metro Conference honors her junior and senior seasons. Finished 11th nationally in kills as a junior. Became the first Bearcat to record 1,000 career kills and 1,000 career digs. Ranked among UC's best in seven categories. Played pivotal role in the turnaround of the program, that after managing just 14 wins over two seasons, had a 16-win year her junior campaign and posted a 27-8 ledger her senior year. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2002.

slots.name: Kenyon Martin
slots.bio: Men’s basketball star who played four seasons at Cincinnati from 1997 to 2000. GoBearcats’ Conference USA Hall of Fame announcement lists Martin as the 2000 consensus National Player of the Year, C-USA Player of the Year, the league’s only three-time Defensive Player of the Year and C-USA Male Athlete of the Decade. He helped UC reach four NCAA Tournaments, led the Bearcats to a No. 1 ranking and became the No. 1 overall pick in the 2000 NBA Draft.

slots.name: Jolinda Lewis-Miller
slots.bio: Women’s basketball standout at Cincinnati from 1994 to 1998. A GoBearcats article notes that Lewis-Miller ranked eighth on UC’s all-time scoring list with 1,523 career points, was a two-time All-Conference USA selection, led the team in scoring for three seasons and led the Bearcats in assists twice. She also earned Great Midwest All-Newcomer honors and CoSIDA Academic All-District First Team recognition.

slots.name: Joe Linneman
slots.bio: Four-sport letterwinner, earning honors in football, basketball, baseball and track. Achieved the most success in football where he was a standout at four different positions during his career. Served as team captain as a senior. Honored for his accomplishments as a punter. Went on to play professional football. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1990.

slots.name: Bob Huggins
slots.bio: Bob Huggins coached Cincinnati men's basketball from 1989 to 2005 and led the Bearcats to the 1992 Final Four. He joined UC's Hall of Fame Class of 2026.

slots.name: Bev Obringer
slots.bio: Dominant post player during her four-plus seasons as a Bearcat. Showed the ability to be a force inside as an alternate in the starting lineup during her freshman year. Emerged to lead the squad in rebounding (9.4) as a sophomore. Missed all but the first two games of the 1987 season due to injury but came back to lead the team in both scoring and rebounding in 1988 and 1989, averaging 17.4 points and 9.1 rebounds as a senior. First team All-Metro Conference her junior and senior years, also earning all-tournament honors in both seasons. Earned honorable mention All-American honors in 1986 (American Women's Sports Federation). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1999.

slots.name: Dr. Nancy Hamant
slots.bio: Associate professor emerita, longtime Faculty Athletics Representative and UC alumna who dedicated her career to the university. Hamant spent 43 years preparing UC students for teaching careers, represented UC with the NCAA and served in Faculty Senate and athletics committee roles. Her GoBearcats profile credits her with helping guide UC’s athletics transition into the BIG EAST and notes her enduring support of student-athlete academic success.

slots.name: Pat Cummings
slots.bio: Set new standards for big men at UC. Closed his career as the No. 2 scorer in UC history with 1,762 points (total currently sixth). Also owned the career mark for field goal percentage (.581), which has since been topped once. Season field goal percentage of .642 set in 1978 remains a UC record. Became a starter his sophomore season and relinquished the role only when sidelined for most of the 1977 season by a fractured ankle. Led the team in scoring his junior and senior seasons, averaging 24.4 points as a senior. Team MVP his junior and senior seasons and tri-captain as a senior. Two-time All-Metro Conference first team selection and league Player of the Year as a senior. Earned All-American recognition as a senior in 1979 (Citizens Savings). Taken in the third round of the 1979 NBA draft by Milwaukee. Played 10 seasons in the NBA. UC Athletics Hall of Fame in 1990.

slots.name: Dr. William Schwarberg
slots.bio: Outstanding running back on the UC football teams of the mid-1930s and also starred in baseball. Following service in the Navy during World War II, he returned to UC and served in just about every capacity in the athletics department until retiring in 1982. Served as head golf coach for 28 years, during which he compiled a 257-69 record in dual meets and developed three NCAA Championships qualifiers. Never had a losing season as head golf coach, at one time posting 47 consecutive victories. Also served stints as head baseball coach, director of intramurals and associate athletic director. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1985.

slots.name: Mardy Gilyard
slots.bio: Electrifying Cincinnati football playmaker who helped lead the Bearcats to back-to-back BIG EAST championships and BCS Bowl appearances in 2008 and 2009. Gilyard was the BIG EAST Special Teams Player of the Year in both seasons and earned First Team All-America honors as both a receiver and kick returner. He finished his UC career ranked first in receptions, receiving touchdowns, receiving yards, all-purpose yards, kickoff returns and kickoff return touchdowns.

slots.name: Dr. Ken Stephens
slots.bio: Longtime team physician for UC Athletics and Assistant Medical Director and Coordinator of Athletic Medicine for University Health Services. A 2008 GoBearcats football media guide said Stephens had served as the Bearcats’ team physician for more than 30 years and worked in college health at UC since 1975. The same guide cited his UC clinical professor roles, national athletic-equipment standards leadership, U.S. Olympic Committee volunteer physician service and founding membership in the American Medical Society for Sports Medicine.

slots.name: Dottie Mueller Braun
slots.plaque_sport_line: BASKETBALL · SWIMMING · RIFLE · ARCHERY · VOLLEYBALL · BOWLING
slots.bio: Distinguished herself both as an outstanding student and fine athlete while in the campus' women's sports programs of the late 1940s. Participated actively in six sports: basketball, swimming, rifle, archery, volleyball and bowling. Earned a UC Blazer, the highest women's athletic award, at the conclusion of her sophomore year. Member of Phi Beta Kappa and Mortar Board. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1981.

slots.name: Greg Cook
slots.bio: One of the nation's most prolific passers of the 1960s. Led the nation in completions (219), passing yards (3,272), total offense (3,210) and touchdowns (25) in 1968. Closed his career as UC's career record-holder for completions (332), attempts (655), passing yards (4,906), and TD passes (34). Set an NCAA record for passing yards in a game with 554 vs. Ohio in 1968. Second team All-American in 1968 (Central Press), also earning honorable mention All-American recognition (AP, UPI, NEA). MVP of the College All-Star Game. Played in the Blue-Gray, American Bowl and Senior Bowl all-star games. Taken with the No. 5 pick by the Cincinnati Bengals in the 1969 draft. Led the American Football Conference in passing and earned Rookie of the Year honors in 1969. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1986. UC Football Ring of Honor.

slots.name: Jim Holstein
slots.bio: Three-sport star of the early 1950s. Led the basketball team in scoring in each of his final three seasons and closed his career at UC's all-time scoring leader (1,146 points). Earned All-Mid-American Conference honors in each of his final three seasons. MVP of the 1951-52 Bearcats. Selected by Minneapolis in the 1952 NBA Draft. Lettered in football and was a standout in baseball. Served stints as a college head basketball coach at St. Joseph's and Ball State. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1980.

slots.name: Jacqueline Keire
slots.bio: Swimming and diving standout for Cincinnati from 2013 to 2017. Keire was a three-time All-American, qualified for the NCAA Championships in all four seasons and was a three-time AAC Most Outstanding Swimmer honoree. She won 13 conference championships, held nearly every UC record in her events and won gold for Team Canada at the 2017 World University Games.

slots.name: Jim Stanley
slots.bio: Twelve-time letterwinner in cross country, indoor track and outdoor track from 1971 to 1974. Stanley qualified three times for the NCAA Cross Country Championships and three times for the NCAA outdoor six-mile run, now the 10,000 meters. He placed fourth in the six mile at the 1973 NCAA Outdoor Championship to earn First Team All-America honors and held UC’s six-mile/10,000-meter record for nearly 40 years.

slots.name: Tony Pike
slots.bio: Quarterback for Cincinnati’s 2008 and 2009 BCS Bowl teams. Pike earned First Team All-BIG EAST honors in 2009 after throwing for 2,520 yards and 29 touchdowns in nine games, and finished his UC career with 5,018 passing yards, 49 touchdowns and a 16-3 record as a starter. He was a team captain and NFL Draft pick.

slots.name: Charlie Keating
slots.bio: First at UC to capture a national championship, winning the 200-yard butterfly at the 1946 NCAA Championships, and in the process, earning All-American honors. Helped team to an eighth place finish at the 1946 NCAAs. Served as team captain in 1947 and 1948. Named UC's Most Outstanding Athlete in 1946. Finished second in the 200 yard breaststroke in 1948. Instrumental in supporting swimming and diving in the Greater Cincinnati area. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1979.

slots.name: Rodney Van Johnson
slots.bio: Nearly a one-man track team, constantly scoring points in the high jump and sprint events. Qualified for the NCAA Championships as a junior, establishing the UC record of 7'3". Also set school records in the 100 meters, 4x100 meter relay and 4x400 meter relay. Champion of the 100 meters, 200 meters and high jump at the 1983 Metro Conference Championships, leading UC to a runner-up finish and earning Most Outstanding Athlete honors. Cleared 6'10" in his very first meet, fulfilling a vow he made to break the school record. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2002.

slots.name: Ron Stapleton
slots.sport: Men's Track & Field, Men's Cross Country
slots.bio: Cross country and track standout recognized in GoBearcats’ track and field history notes as Cincinnati’s first cross country All-American. Stapleton placed 23rd at the 1971 NCAA Cross Country Championships, which the same GoBearcats history page identified as UC’s top NCAA cross country finish at the time.

slots.name: Keely Feeman
slots.bio: Three-year starter and four-year regular on the teams of the mid-1980s. Team's second-leading scorer her sophomore and junior seasons and led UC in scoring as a senior(18.9). Led the nation in field goal accuracy as a senior, establishing a UC record (.927). First team All-Metro Conference as a senior. Team co-captain as a senior. Closed her career as the No. 3 career scoring leader (1,728). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1996.

slots.name: Thomas Thacker
slots.bio: Distinguished himself as a starter on UC's 1961 NCAA Championship team, then took on a leadership role in the 1962 national title run and the 1963 runner-up finish. Closed his career in ninth place on UC's career scoring list with 1,152 points. Three-time All-Missouri Valley Conference selection. Earned consensus All-American honors in 1963 and was a second team AP All-American selection. Territorial selection in the 1963 NBA Draft by the Cincinnati Royals. Played in the pros for seven seasons with Cincinnati, Boston and Indiana. Is the only player in basketball history to win NCAA, ABA and NBA championships. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1981.

slots.name: Ralph Richter M.D.
slots.bio: Four-year letterman and two-season starter on the successful UC teams of the late 1940s. Became a starter as a sophomore and led the team in scoring (13.5 points). Leading scorer (16.4) on the 1948-49 team that posted a then-best record of 23-4 and became the first UC team to achieve a national ranking. Earned first team All-Mid-American Conference honors as a junior. Helped UC compile a 77-27 record during his career. Finished with 1,053 career points. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1989.

slots.name: Gino Guidugli
slots.bio: Former Cincinnati quarterback, James P. Kelly Athletics Hall of Fame member and Nippert Stadium Ring of Honor member. GoBearcats lists Guidugli as holding UC career records for passing yards, attempts, completions and touchdown passes at the time of his staff profile, along with single-season records for passing yards, attempts and completions. He was the only UC quarterback listed with a 3,500-yard passing season and 14 career 300-yard passing games.

slots.name: Bill Keating Jr.
slots.bio: Followed in the footsteps of his father (William) and uncle (Charles), both members of UC's Athletic Hall of Fame, to achieve success as a swimmer and provide leadership as a student. Led the UC teams of the mid-1970s to four consecutive league championships. Qualified for the NCAA Championships in each of his four seasons. Served as captain his junior and senior campaigns. Set UC record for most points scored during his career. Closed his career holding seven school records and five league records in seven different events. Elected team MVP his freshman and sophomore seasons--the award was not present his junior and senior years. Recipient of the Jimmy Nippert Award as the outstanding senior male student-athlete. Inducted into Sophos, Sigma Sigma and Metro honoraries and served as president of Sigma Sigma. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1992.

slots.name: Jason Maxiell
slots.bio: Earned four varsity letters for UC from 2001-2005. Ranks 2nd in UC history for consecutive games played with 129. Ranks 2nd in UC history for blocked shots with 252. While at UC amassed 1,566 points which ranks 12th all-time in school history. Two-time All-Conference USA performer. Drafted by the Detroit Pistons in the 1st Round(26th overall) in the 2005 National Basketball Association Draft.

slots.name: Jeff Johnson
slots.bio: Cross country and distance standout who was the epitome of the term "student-athlete" during his time at UC. Captured the Metro Conference title in the 1,500 at the 1983 league championships. No. 1 runner in cross country in all three of his final seasons. Set six indoor and five outdoor distance records. Electrical engineering major who graduated Magna Cum Laude. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1997.

slots.name: Dan Hoard
slots.bio: Known as the Voice of the Bearcats, Hoard handled play-by-play duties for Cincinnati football and men’s basketball and hosted UC radio and television programming. His GoBearcats profile describes him as one of UC’s great ambassadors and notes his work as radio announcer for the Cincinnati Bengals and fill-in host for the Cincinnati Reds. He was inducted into the James P. Kelly Athletics Hall of Fame in 2019.

slots.name: Trish Ladusaw
slots.bio: Four-year volleyball letterwinner from 1999 to 2002 who finished her Cincinnati career with 2,074 digs, then the second-most in NCAA history. Ladusaw owned every UC dig record at graduation and still held the school marks for career digs and digs per set in the archived GoBearcats profile. She also joined UC’s 1,000 kill-1,000 dig club and helped the Bearcats go 98-34 with four postseason appearances.

slots.name: Al Rubenstein
slots.bio: Four-year starter and steady backcourt performer on the basketball teams of the late 1940s. Tallied 303 points as a freshman, a record at the time. Became noted for his ball handling wizardry, particularly in the closing minutes of games. First team All-Mid-American Conference selection his sophomore and junior seasons. Scored 987 career points. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1995.

slots.name: Bob Wiesenhan
slots.bio: Key forward on Cincinnati’s 1960-61 national championship team. GoBearcats’ national championship history notes that Wiesenhahn led UC in scoring at 17.1 points per game, helped the Bearcats finish 27-3 and win their first NCAA men’s basketball title, and finished third in NCAA all-tournament team voting behind Jerry Lucas and teammate Carl Bouldin.

slots.name: Geoff Hensley
slots.bio: One of UC's top golfers of all time. Earned four letters in golf and was a regular contributor throughout his career. Qualified for the NCAA Championships as a sophomore. Was UC's top scorer in dual match competition in each of his final three seasons. Later recognized as one of the top teaching pros in the Cincinnati area. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1991.

slots.name: Ethan Allen
slots.bio: Three-sport standout at UC, lettering in basketball, track and baseball. His .473 batting average in 1926 was a UC record until recent years when the increase in games played merited an increase in the minimum number of at-bats. Signed with the Cincinnati Reds upon the completion of college and went straight to the major leagues to begin his 13-year professional career. Closed his pro career with a .300 batting average, 47 home runs, 501 RBIs and 84 stolen bases. Began a 23-year stint as head coach at Yale University where he guided his 1947 and 1948 teams to the College World Series, with future president George Bush playing first base. Elected to the American Association of College Baseball Coaches Hall of Fame in 1970 and the Ohio Baseball Hall of Fame in 1966. Member of the UC Athletic Hall of Fame charter class of inductees.

slots.name: Tom Marvaso
slots.bio: Cincinnati football standout from 1973 to 1975 and a UC Ring of Honor inductee. Marvaso was a Sporting News First Team All-American in 1975, ranked among UC’s top five career punt returners and was named team MVP in 1974. He scored on both an interception return and kickoff return in the same game, played in the East-West Shrine Game and Senior Bowl and was drafted into the NFL.

slots.name: Jack Laub
slots.bio: Known as “Black Cat,” Laub is listed by GoBearcats as the only student-athlete in NCAA history to play six varsity years and as Cincinnati’s first basketball assistant coach. After playing at City College of New York and serving in World War II, he came to UC in 1946, helped the Bearcats win four straight MAC titles from 1947 to 1950 and later served as an assistant, scout and assistant director of intramurals.

slots.name: Joe Morrison
slots.bio: Long before he attained the title "Mr. Versatility" as a professional, he demonstrated his variety of skills as a Bearcat. Began his career as a quarterback, leading the team in passing as a freshman. Moved to halfback as a sophomore and was the team's top ground-gainer his junior campaign. Also led UC in receiving in 1958 and was the team scoring leader his freshman and junior seasons. Rugged member of the secondary who led UC in interceptions in three of his four seasons. Returned a pair of interceptions for touchdowns as a freshman, scoring from 87 and 88 yards. Held UC career interception return yardage record when he graduated, a mark since tied. Closed his career as UC's all-time leading scorer (127 points). Earned All-Missouri Valley Conference honors as a sophomore. Played in the North-South, Senior Bowl and College All-Star games. Selected in the third round of the 1959 NFL Draft by the New York Giants and continued to display his versatility during his 13 seasons with the club, setting team records as a receiver. Successful head coach on the major college level. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1978.

slots.name: Honza Vitazka
slots.bio: Standout swimmer at UC from 1996-1999. Lettered all four years at UC. Six time All-American while here at UC. Holds UC records in the 200 IM, 400 IM, 200 butterfly and also 6 Czech Republic national team records. Competed in the 100 butterfly, 200 and 400 individual medleys for his native Czech Republic in the 2000 Sydney Olympics.

slots.name: Roy Lagaly
slots.bio: Recorded top-10 finishes at the 1942 NCAA Championships in the 100, 200 and 440 yard freestyle events. Following service in World War II, returned to UC to earn All-American honors with a fourth place finish in the 1,500 yard freestyle at the 1946 NCAA Championships, helping UC to an eighth place finish. Served as team captain of the 1948 Bearcats. Following a successful coaching career in area high schools, returned to UC in 1964 as head swim coach. Compiled a 70-50 dual meet record as a head coach and directed UC to six consecutive Missouri Valley Conference championships, a streak broken by the school's departure from the conference. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1983.

slots.name: Bob Hynes
slots.bio: Did not play football until his senior year--his coop work assignment as part of his engineering studies presenting conflicts--but made a lasting impact when he did finally take up the sport. Worked his way into the lineup by mid-season. Intercepted four passes--a UC record--and spearheaded a 15-7 win over Ohio Northern. Rushed for 307 yards--a mark which still stands as a UC record--to lead a 69-0 romp over Case a week later. Scored five touchdowns in the final three contests of the 1923 season. Distinguished in baseball, serving as a regular his final two seasons. Batted .426 and served as team captain as a senior. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2001.

slots.name: Ann Thomas
slots.bio: All-American forward for Cincinnati women’s soccer from 1997 to 2001. Thomas was twice named to the Conference USA all-conference team, including first-team honors in 2001, and was an all-freshman selection in 1998. She helped UC go 10-0 in conference play, win the 2001 regular-season Conference USA championship and advance to the Round of 16 in the NCAA Women’s College Cup.

slots.name: John Pease
slots.bio: Outstanding football player who continued his love of the Bearcats through lifetime support of the program. Three-year letterwinner as a rugged lineman. Team captain as a senior. Inducted into the Sigma Sigma honorary. One of the founders of UNOCIN, an early organization that raised financial support for football. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1980.

slots.name: Dr. Richard Goist
slots.bio: Four-year starter who helped UC compile a 35-5-1 record and two Mid-American Conference titles. Earned All-Mid-American Conference honors as both a junior and a senior. Three-time All-Ohio selection. Moved from defensive back to halfback as a junior and set the UC season record for yards per carry (8.77). Team captain and MVP as a senior. His number, 62, was retired at the close of his career. Honorable mention All-American as both a junior in 1953 and a senior in 1954. Played in the East-West Shrine and Senior Bowl all-star games. Selected in the 12th round of the 1955 NFL draft by Detoit. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1986.

slots.name: Danny McCoin
slots.bio: Three-year starter. Co-captain as a senior and a natural team leader. Holds UC records for season (.642) and career (.605) completion percentage. Concluded his career holding the UC career records for completions (544), attempts (899), passing yards (6,801) and TD passes (39) and remains among the top three in each category. Threw for 2,831 yards and 13 TDs as a junior and 2,031 yards and 13 scores as a senior. Two-time Metro Conference Football All-Stars selection. Honorable mention All-American in 1986 (AP). Drafted in the 11th round of the 1988 NFL draft by Cincinnati and played on season with Detroit. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2003.

slots.name: Gary Heinrich
slots.bio: UC's first swimmer to earn All-American honors in three successive seasons. Claimed a total of six All-American awards competing in three NCAA Championships. Posted a runner-up finish in the 200 yard butterfly at the 1961 NCAAs as a sophomore, also finishing third in the 1500 yard freestyle and fourth in the 400 yard freestyle, giving him three All-American awards; his point total in that meet was responsible for UC's ninth place finish. Helped UC to a seventh place finish in the 1962 NCAA Championships with runner-up finishes in the 1500 and 400 yard freestyles. Capped his UC career with a fifth place finish in the 1,650 yard freestyle at the 1963 NCAAs. Served as team captain as a senior. Closed his career holding 10 UC records. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1989.

slots.name: Jonathan Ruffin
slots.bio: Winner of the 2000 Lou Groza Award, which is presented annually to the top football placekicker. UC's first-ever consensus first-team All-America selection in 2000. Holds school records for career points (315) and extra points made (129). Ranks first in UC history for field goals made (62), field goal percentage (.785) and consecutive field goals made (13). One of the few football players to have played in the National Football League (NFL), NFL Europe, Canadian Football League (CFL) and Arena Football League.

slots.name: Loretta Blaut
slots.bio: High jumper Loretta Blaut earned six All-America honors and finished second at both NCAA championships in 2018. She joined UC's Hall of Fame Class of 2026.

slots.name: Josh Schneider
slots.bio: One of the most decorated swimmers in Cincinnati history. Schneider won the 2010 NCAA title in the 50 freestyle, making him UC’s most recent NCAA champion in the archived GoBearcats profile. He was a five-time All-American, seven-time BIG EAST champion and two-time BIG EAST Male Swimmer of the Year, and left UC with five school records.

slots.name: Ken Byers
slots.bio: Two-way performer at offensive and defensive tackle, earning All-Missouri Valley Conference honors his junior and senior seasons. Three-year starter. Co-captain of 1961 team. Claude Rost Award as team MVP in 1961. Second team All-American in 1961 (Williamson Ratings). Played in the 1962 College All-Star Game. Seventh round draft pick by the New York Giants in 1962. Closed his professional career with Minnesota. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1983.

slots.name: Phil Wheeler
slots.bio: Three-year starter in basketball, helping the teams compile a 49-25 record. Second-leading scorer as a junior on the team that reached the semifinals of the NIT. Team captain and leading scorer (21.5 points) as a senior. Closed his career in the 1,000 Point Club with 1,055 career points. Averaged 11.8 rebounds as a senior and 10.5 during his career. Selected by the Philadelphia Warriors in the 1956 NBA Draft. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1989.

slots.name: Roger Stephens
slots.bio: Three-year letterwinner and key rusher as a halfback on the 1946-47-48 teams. Helped those squads compile a 19-11-1 record, win one Mid-American Conference title and make the school's first bowl game appearance. Was the team's rushing leader in 1946 and 1947, gaining 959 yards and scoring seven TDs in 1947. Held the career rushing record when he completed his career. His 6.65 yards-per-carry average remains a UC career record. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1986.

slots.name: Rick Roberson
slots.bio: Three-year starter on the Bearcat teams of the late 1960s. Led the team in both scoring and rebounding in each of his three seasons, a feat accomplished by only one other player, Oscar Robertson. Team MVP as a sophomore. Two-time All-Missouri Valley Conference selection. Averaged a double-double for his career (15.8 points, 12.4 rebounds) and finished with 1,196 career points. Taken in the first round by Los Angeles in the 1969 NBA draft and played in the pro ranks for 13 seasons. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1997.

slots.name: Ann Degenstein
slots.bio: Women’s swimming and diving standout, seven-time Conference USA champion and member of the C-USA All-Decade Team. Degenstein was the 2005 C-USA Swimmer of the Year and earned All-America honors with an 11th-place finish in the 100 butterfly and 14th-place finish in the 200 butterfly at the 2005 NCAA Championship. At graduation, she held the C-USA and UC records in both butterfly events and earned major academic honors.

slots.name: Barb Jaksa
slots.bio: Four-year starter who provided excellent court leadership as well as a scoring presence. Averaged 15.4 points and 4.3 assists while helping the 1980-81 team compile a best-ever 27-9 record and make the school's first postseason tournament appearance, reaching the National Women's Invitational Tournament. Led UC in assists in each of her final two seasons. Topped the 1,000 mark in career scoring and closed her career No. 2 on UC's career scoring list. Named to the Metro Conference All-Tournament Team in both her junior and senior seasons. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1992.

slots.name: Olga Weil
slots.plaque_sport_line: BASKETBALL · TENNIS- RIFLE · HOCKEY - TRACK · SWIMMING · GOLF
slots.bio: Very active participant in the women's sports program. Played on the successful women's basketball teams of the early 1920s for four seasons. Participated for two years each in tennis, rifle, track and baseball and had seasons in swimming and field hockey. Recipient of the C Ring as the outstanding female senior student on the UC campus. Standout in the local amateur tennis and golf competition following graduation. Won he Cincinnati Metro Golf title 13 times and three Ohio amateur championships. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1982.

slots.name: Nicholas "Nick" Shundich
slots.bio: Four-year member of the football teams, earning freshman numerals in 1948 and varsity letters in 1949-50-51. Served as co-captain as a senior, providing leadership to the team that finished with a 10-1 record. Was a mainstay on the offensive line at tackle. Helped UC to a record of 25-9 and a pair of Mid-American Conference championships during his three seasons on varsity. Played on two UC bowl teams, the 1949 Glass Bowl champions and the 1950 Sun Bowl runners-up. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1988.

slots.name: Michelle MacPherson Hojnacki
slots.bio: Was a medalist at the 1984 Olympics competing for her native country Canada. Qualified for the NCAA Championships in each of her four seasons at UC. Team MVP and leading scorer her sophomore and junior seasons. Won a total of 14 individual and relay event titles at the National Independent Championship meets during her career, leading UC to the meet title in 1987. Won nine All-American awards. Closed her career holding seven school records in the freestyles, individual medleys and medley relays. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2000.

slots.name: Bill Schnier
slots.plaque_sport_line: TOS &WAOTEN STRACK & FELDO CROS COUNTRY COACH
slots.bio: Legendary Cincinnati track and field and cross country head coach for 33 years, from 1980 to 2013. GoBearcats credits Schnier with coaching 136 individual conference champions, 25 NCAA national meet qualifiers, 10 All-Americans, two Olympic medalists and 12 conference-title teams. He earned conference coach of the year honors 15 times and was inducted into UC’s James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2012.

slots.name: Mike Woods
slots.bio: Cincinnati football’s first consensus First Team All-American after a 114-tackle senior season in 1977. Woods was team MVP in 1976, a two-time captain and a Senior Bowl selection before the Baltimore Colts selected him in the second round of the 1978 NFL Draft. He played 48 NFL games, including 32 starts, before his career was cut short after he was paralyzed in a 1982 shooting.

slots.name: Larry Elsasser
slots.bio: Outstanding hitter and fielder on the UC baseball teams of the early 1960s. Led Bearcats in hitting as a sophomore (.337). Established what was recognized as a modern-day record for season batting average (.426) while leading UC in hitting as a senior. Was ranked seventh nationally in hitting (.426) and fifth in slugging percentage (.734) as a senior. Earned first team All-Missouri Valley Conference honors in each of his three seasons. Reserve on the UC basketball teams, playing on the 1962 NCAA Championship team and the 1963 team that posted a runner-up finish. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1989.

slots.name: Julie Dupont-Fitzgerald
slots.bio: Volleyball standout Julie DuPont became Cincinnati’s first volleyball All-American when the AVCA named her a third-team All-American in 2003. GoBearcats also noted she was the Conference USA Player of the Year, a first-team all-region selection and the league leader in kills and points per game. She set UC single-season records in kills and kills per game while helping the Bearcats to a C-USA regular-season championship share and NCAA Tournament appearance.

slots.name: Frank Shaut
slots.bio: Likely UC's greatest wrestler of all-time. Posted a perfect 51-0 record in the 177-pound class in dual meet competition and had a career mark of 55-3 with the inclusion of postseason championship competition. Earned team MVP honors in each of his four seasons. Began his career with an 11-0 mark as a freshman. Extended his streak to 24 straight wins as a sophomore, suffering his first loss at the NCAA Championships. Repeated his 13-0 record as a junior and advanced to the second round at the NCAA Championships. Capped his career with a 14-0 mark as a senior. Returned following graduation to serve as head wrestling coach for three seasons. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1988.

slots.name: Miriam Merrill
slots.bio: Track and field thrower recognized by GoBearcats as UC’s first female track and field All-American. Merrill placed in the weight throw in 2001 and, according to later GoBearcats coverage, her 2001 weight throw mark stood as the school record for 17 years before Annette Echikunwoke broke it in 2018.

slots.name: Tony Yates
slots.bio: Three-year starter at point guard was called "my coach on the floor" by then-head coach Ed Jucker for his leadership. Directed UC to an 82-7 record, NCAA national titles in 1961 and 1962 and a near miss of a third straight crown in 1963. Three-year winner of the team's Best Defensive Player award for his efforts in helping UC finish 15th in 1961, fourth in 1962 and first in 1963 in the NCAA national defensive rankings. Team captain as a senior. First team All-Missouri Valley Conference choice in 1963. Earned second team (Helms) and honorable mention (UPI) All-American recognition in 1962. Was a first team All-American (Helms Foundation), earning third team honors (AP, NABC) and honorable mention laurels (UPI, Sporting News) in 1963. Returned to UC to launch his coach career as an assistant coach 1972-74. Served as UC head basketball coach for six seasons (1984-89), compiling a 70-100 record. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1985.

slots.name: Herb Jones
slots.bio: Two-year starter for Cincinnati after transferring from junior college. Jones led the 1991-92 NCAA Final Four team in scoring and rebounding at 18.1 points and 7.1 rebounds per game. He became the only Bearcat to reach the 1,000-point club in just two UC seasons, finished with 1,097 points and 475 rebounds, and earned Associated Press honorable mention All-America honors in 1992.

slots.name: Joy Roberts Bachman
slots.bio: Four-season performer and starter her final three seasons. Team MVP her junior and senior years. UC scoring leader as a junior (12.9) and rebounding champ as a senior (7.3). Concluded her career No. 3 on the career scoring list with 1,215 points and was the No. 3 rebounder (674). Recipient of the Helen Norman Smith Award as the top female senior student-athlete in 1983. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1993.

slots.name: Glenn Sample
slots.bio: Multi-sport standout who was a fixture at third base for almost his entire UC career. Earned All-Mid-American Conference and All-Ohio honors as a linebacker in football. Turned down professional opportunities in both football and baseball to fulfill service commitment. Returned to UC in 1956 as an assistant football coach, embarking on a career in which he served, sometimes concurrently, as head wrestling coach, intramural director and assistant athletics director. Began a 21-season career as head baseball coach in 1961, directing his very first team to the NCAA district tournament. His teams won three Missouri Valley Conference titles and made four NCAA Tournament appearances. His jersey number, 1, was retired. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1982.

slots.name: Ike Stewart
slots.plaque_sport_line: FOOTBALL · TENNIS · BASKETBALL - SWIMMING · BASEBALL · GYM · TRACK
slots.bio: One of the great all-sports standouts of the early century. Earned a total of 15 letters in football, basketball, track, swimming, tennis and gym while attaining his undergraduate degree in electrical engineering. Active in many campus organizations. Had a great love and interest in flying and after graduation became a pilot. Pioneered air mail service between Cincinnati and Chicago. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1982.

slots.name: Bob Meier
slots.bio: Three-year letterwinner in football. Played center on offense and linebacker on defense on the teams of the early 1940s. Never missed a minute of playing time due to injury. Voted team MVP by his teammates. Also lettered in track and field, specializing in the pole vault. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1992.

slots.name: Dick Dallmer
slots.bio: Earned team Most Valuable Player honors in each of his three seasons on the Bearcat varsity. Closed his career in 1950 as UC's all-time scoring leader with 1,098 points though he did not lead the team in scoring in any of his three seasons. First team All-Mid-American Conference selection in 1950. Team co-captain as a junior and captain as a senior. First Bearcat to earn All-American honors in basketball, earning honorable mention in 1948 (AP) and 1949 (AP) and third team laurels in 1950 (AP). Selected by Philadelphia in the 1950 NBA draft. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1984.

slots.name: Meridy Glenn
slots.bio: Longtime Cincinnati women’s soccer head coach from 1984 to 2007. Glenn built a 255-win program with six NCAA Tournament appearances, including a 2001 Sweet 16 run, three regular-season conference championships and five conference tournament titles. She was the 2001 Conference USA Coach of the Year, became the first female Division I coach to reach 200 career wins and coached five All-Americans and 42 all-conference honorees.

slots.name: 1961-62 Men's Basketball
slots.bio: Cincinnati's 1961-62 men's basketball team won the 1962 NCAA championship, the program's second consecutive national title under Ed Jucker. UC's 2012 induction announcement identifies this championship team as a Hall of Fame inductee.

slots.name: Bill Westerfeld
slots.bio: World War II veteran who entered UC following the war and made an immediate impact on the basketball court. Led the team in scoring his freshman and sophomore seasons. Team captain his junior and senior years, helping direct UC to a 40-12 record during those two years and a 65-34 ledger and three Mid-American Conference titles during his career. Earned All-Mid-American Conference honors as a sophomore. Closed his career with 1,092 points, becoming UC's first 1,000-point scorer. Selected as the most outstanding senior male student-athlete and received the Mr. Bearcat Award as UC's top senior male student. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1990.

slots.name: Andrew Kean
slots.bio: Earned UC's first Men's Soccer All-American selection in 1998 and 1999. Conference USAAll-Freshman selection. Lead UC to its first National Tournament appearance in 1998. 1999 Ohio Player of the Year. Earned Conference USA Defensive Player of the Year in 1999 and All-Region accolades in both 1998 and 1999.

slots.name: David Canary
slots.bio: Two way starter at end on the 1957-58-59 teams. Earned the John Pease Award as the team's most outstanding lineman in 1958 and 1959, beating out teammates Ron Kostelnik, Jim Leo, Max Messner and Ken Byers--all of whom went on to the pro ranks. Named to the Pop Warner Academic All-American Team as a senior. Drafted by Denver of the fledgling American Football League but the College Conservative of Music graduate turned down pro football to launch his acting career. Became a regular on the TV series Bonanza and is a member of the cast of the Emmy-winning daytime drama All My Children. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2005.

slots.name: Reggie Taylor
slots.bio: Mighty-might (5'7") who emerged as UC's all-time leading rusher over his four-year career as a starter. Topped the 1000-yard mark in each of his last three seasons, the only Bearcat to do so. Had 21 century rushing games, a school record, and 24 rushing touchdowns. Gained 1,325 yards on 256 carries as a senior--the season yardage total surpassed by one play in the UC record book. Holds UC career records for rushing attempts (876) and rushing yards (4,242). Metro Conference Player of the Year in both his junior and senior seasons and a three-time member of the league's football all-stars team. Winner of the 1987 Jimmy Nippert Award as the university's top senior athlete. Honorable mention All-American in each of his final three seasons (1984: AP, 1985: AP, 1986: AP, Sporting News). Played in the 1987 East-West Shrine All-Star Game. Taken in the 11th round of the 1987 NFL draft by Cincinnati and played for Tampa Bay before moving to the Canadian Football League where he played for British Columbia. Jersey number (30) retired. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1997.

slots.name: Kathy Klump
slots.bio: Middle-distance runner for Cincinnati track and field from 2008 to 2012. Klump was a three-time All-American, four-time BIG EAST champion and the 2012 BIG EAST Most Outstanding Indoor Track Performer. She earned First Team All-America honors in 2012 with top-six NCAA finishes in the 800 meters and set five school records, including indoor and outdoor 800-meter marks.

slots.name: Charlie Casuto
slots.bio: Attained national honors as UC's diving coach. Tutored 10 divers who earned a total of 32 All-American awards during his 23-year career. Attracted international acclaim when Becky Ruehl capped her freshman season by finishing fourth in the platform diving competition at the 1996 Olympics. Coached two national diving champions, Pat Evans, who won the men's 3-meter title at the 1989 NCAA Championships, and Becky Ruehl, who won the platform title in 1996. Twice named NCAA Diving Coach of the Year. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1997.

slots.name: Jill Webster McCambridge
slots.bio: One of the first females to earn an athletics grant-in-aid at UC. UC's first four-time All-American with her finishes at the Association of Intercollegiate Athletics for Women Championships. Won three state titles at the Ohio Association of Intercollegiate Athletics for Women Championships and was twice the meet's high point diver. Received the Monica Nolan Award as the team MVP in each of her four seasons. Presented the Helen Norman Smith Award in 1981 as UC's top senior female student-athlete. Finished fifth at the 1980 U.S. Outdoor Championships. Qualified for the 1984 U.S. Olympic Trials. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1991.

slots.name: Will Stargel
slots.bio: One of the first African-American standouts of the UC football program. Came to UC in 1941 and contributed to the 1942 squad's 8-2 season. Served with the Fifth Army overseas during World War II. Returned to continue his athletic and academic career in 1946, helping the Bearcats compile a 9-2 record which featured a win over defending Big Ten champion Indiana to open the season and a victory over Virginia Tech in the Sun Bowl. Also lettered in basketball and track. Set UC records in the low and high hurdles which stood until broken by his son, Scott, in the 1960s. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1979.

slots.name: Becky Ruehl Amann
slots.bio: Five-time All-American as a diver. Became UC's first female national champion in any sport when she won the platform diving at the 1996 NCAA Championships as a freshman. Won titles on both the one-meter and three-meter boards at the National Independent Championships as a prelude to the NCAAs. Captured the hearts as well as the attention of America at the 1996 Olympics when she finished fourth in the platform diving competition. Earned All-American honors in three-meter diving at the NCAAs her sophomore and junior seasons. Came back after a year off due to injury to garner All-American honors in the platform diving as a senior. Champion in the classroom that had to balance her time-demanding major, graphic design, with athletics, but did so successfully to earn first team Academic All-American honors (CoSIDA). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2005.

slots.name: Jim Ard
slots.bio: Three-year regular who earned first team All-Missouri Valley Conference honors in each of those three campaigns. Was named Missouri Valley Conference Sophomore of the Year in 1968. UC Most Valuable Player his junior and senior seasons. Missouri Valley Conference Player of the Year in 1970, during which he led UC in scoring (19.2) and rebounding (15.2). Tied the UC single game record for blocked shots (10) which he shares today. Closed his career with 1,256 points and 941 rebounds. Honorable mention All-American in 1970 (AP, UPI). Selected in the first round by Seattle in the 1970 NBA Draft with the sixth pick overall. Played nine seasons of professional basketball. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1996.

slots.name: 2009 Football Team
slots.bio: The 2009 Bearcats went 12-1 overall and 7-0 in the BIG EAST, finished No. 3 in the final BCS standings and completed the program’s first undefeated regular season of the modern era. Under BIG EAST Coach of the Year Brian Kelly, UC won its second straight BIG EAST championship, featured Special Teams Player of the Year Mardy Gilyard and placed 11 players on all-conference teams.

slots.name: Sid Gillman
slots.bio: Sid Gillman was the architect of what is considered the greatest era of UC football. His teams compiled a 50-13-1 record in six seasons, won three Mid-American Conference championships and played in a pair of bowl games. Originator of the passing game now considered the West Coast Offense, Gillman began developing that attack while at UC, earning national aerial game rankings. Left UC to become head coach of the Los Angeles Rams and launch a pro coaching career. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1981.

slots.name: Bill Lammert
slots.bio: Standout performer and team leader on the UC squads of the mid-1950s. Four-year letterwinner and starter for his final three seasons. Second-leading scorer as a junior (15.3 points). Team captain and second-leading scorer as a senior (13.4). Helped 1954-55 team to a 21-8 record and a third place finish at the NIT. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1988.

slots.name: Ron Kostelnik
slots.bio: One of UC's top interior linemen of all-time. Played in the North-South college all-star game at the conclusion of his UC career. Taken in the second round of the 1961 NFL draft by Green Bay where he became an anchor on the defensive line of the successful Packer teams of the 1960s. Contributed to Green Bay's NFL titles in 1961, 1962 and 1965 and helped the Packers win the first two Super Bowls in 1966 and 1967. Member of the Baltimore Colts' 1969 NFL title team. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1985.

slots.name: Bob Stratton
slots.bio: UC's leading rusher in 1950, running for 539 yards and five touchdowns. Led team in scoring as a sophomore in 1949 with six TDs for 36 points. Earned All-Mid-American Conference honors his junior and senior seasons. Honorable mention All-American in 1951. Played for Toronto in the Canadian Football League. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1989.

slots.name: Sandy Koufax
slots.bio: Played one season under coach Ed Jucker in 1954. During his one season at UC, he recorded a 3-1 record and a 2.81 earned run average for the Bearcats. Signed professional contract with the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1954. Youngest player ever to be inducted into the Major League Baseball Hall of Fame in 1972 at 36 years old. Named to Major League Baseball's All-Century Team in 1999. Honored by Sporting News as one of the "100 Greatest Baseball Players".

slots.name: Mike Kinnett
slots.bio: First baseman Mike Kinnett was a two-time all-conference selection and finished his UC career with a .372 batting average. He joined the Hall of Fame Class of 2026.

slots.name: 1960-61 Men's Basketball
slots.bio: Cincinnati's 1960-61 men's basketball team finished 27-3 and defeated Ohio State 70-65 to win the program's first NCAA championship. The team was selected for induction into the UC Athletics Hall of Fame in 2011.

slots.name: Dr. Fred W. Heinold
slots.bio: Played several different positions on the UC football teams of the early 1920s and was one of the school's premiere track and field stars. Entered UC's College of Medicine upon graduation in 1921 and simultaneously served as assistant coach while earning his medical degree. Was a successful practicing physician in Cincinnati. Served as president of the Cincinnati Board of Education, President of the UC Alumni Association and was a high school sports official. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1985.

slots.name: Monty Hopkins
slots.bio: Standout swimmer for the Bearcats from 1979-1978. Two-time conference champion, two-time NCAA qualifier and a 1976 Olympic Trials qualifier. Team co-captain during his senior year. Recipient of the Jimmy Nippert Award, which recognizes UC's top male student-athlete. Has been the head coach of the men's and women's swimming and diving teams since 1989. During his tenure, UC has totaled 12 conference team championships, two NCAA individual champions, 17 All-Americans, 14 Academic All-Americans and three Olympians.

slots.name: Bill Talbert
slots.bio: Known nationally as "Mr. Tennis". Ohio high school state singles and doubles champion at Hughes High, across from the UC campus. Finished second in the singles competition at the 1939 NCAA Championships. Also qualified for the doubles competition at the 1939 NCAAs. Member of the U.S. Davis Cup Team in 1946, 1948, 1949, 1951, 1953 and 1953, winning the doubles competition on the 1948 and 1949 victorious U.S. teams. Captain of five Davis Cup Teams (1953-57), compiling a 13-4 record. Captured four doubles titles, four mixed doubles crowns and was singles runner-up twice at the U.S. Championships, later known as the U.S. Open. Won the French Open and Italian Open doubles titles in 1950, teaming with UC product Tony Trabert. Won a total of 33 national titles and was ranked in the USLTA singles top ten 13 gtimes. Named to the National Lawn Tennis Hall of Fame (1967), Hamilton County Sports Hall of Fame (1972), College Tennis Hall of Fame (1984) and the Cincinnati Hall of Fame (2002). First person with diabetes to compete internationally in athletic competition. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1979.

slots.name: Joe Miller
slots.bio: One of the top running backs of the 1950s. Originally enrolled at UC in 1949 but joined the service after one year and served in the Korean conflict. Returned to UC in 1953 upon discharge from the military and immediately became a mainstay on the football teams. Recorded the longest run from scrimmage in UC history--91 yards--vs. Xavier that season, a record that still stands. Rushed for a team-leading 717 yards and 11 touchdowns in 1954, helping UC to an 8-2 record. Captain of the 1955 team. Lettered as a catcher in baseball, earning All-Ohio honors. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1991.

slots.name: Antwan Peek
slots.bio: Three-year starter at defensive end who helped Cincinnati reach three straight bowl games and win its first conference title in nearly 40 years. Peek was a two-time First Team All-Conference USA selection, three-time John Pease Award winner and team co-MVP on the 2002 Conference USA championship team. He is UC’s all-time leader in sacks, tackles for loss, forced fumbles and blocked kicks, and played five NFL seasons after being drafted by Houston.

slots.name: Frank Middendorf
slots.bio: Called by head coach Sid Gillman "the greatest offensive center in the country." Three-year starter. Was an All-Ohio and All-Mid-American Conference selection his junior and senior seasons. Voted the team's Most Efficient Lineman in 1950 and honored as the Bearcats' most valuable offensive player in 1950 and 1951. Played in the Blue-Gray and Senior Bowl all-star games in 1951. Honorable mention All-American in 1951 (AP, UPI, Colliers). Selected by the Washington Redskins in the 1952 NFL draft. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1992.

slots.name: Caroline Cooper
slots.bio: Native of Great Britain and member of that country's national team made a big splash during her career as a Bearcat. Dominated the Metro Conference Championships, going undefeated in all 13 events in which she competed during her four seasons and earned league Female Swimmer of the Year honors all four years. Versatile swimmer who earned a total of 12 All-American awards at the NCAA Championships in the 50 and 100 yard freestyles, the 100 yard butterfly and the 200, 400 and 800 freestyle relays. All-time UC bests posted in the 50 and 100 yard freestyles and the 100 yard butterfly. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1999.

slots.name: Tay Baker
slots.bio: Sixth man on the 1948-49-50 basketball teams that compiled a 60-18 record and won three Mid-American Conference titles. Returned to UC as assistant basketball coach in 1959 after coaching in the high school ranks for nine years. His 1959-60 freshman team posted a best-ever 14-1 record. Became Ed Jucker's assistant with the varsity in 1960-61 and helped guide UC to back-to-back NCAA titles over the next two seasons. Succeeded Jucker as head coach in 1965-66. Directed his initial team to the Missouri Valley Conference title and an NCAA Tournament appearance where UC lost to eventual national champion Texas-El Paso. Compiled a 125-60 record in seven seasons as head coach. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1996.

slots.name: Jim O'Brien
slots.bio: Dual threat whose career is well-document in the receiving and kicking records. Three-year regular who led the team in scoring his junior and senior seasons. Leading receiver, in terms of yardage, all three seasons and tops on the squad in receptions his sophomore and senior years. First receiver to top the 1,000-yard mark in season receiving yards, gaining 1,107 on 44 catches in 1968 to set the season record for yards-per-catch (25.16). Concluded career second in receptions (104) and first in receiving yards (2,285), TD receptions (21) and yards-per-catch (21.97), the latter two remain as records. Led nation in scoring in 1968 with a UC season record 142 points. Career scoring leader (142 points) and holds the record for most games scored in (24). Claude Rost Award as team MVP as a senior. Honorable mention All-American in both 1968 (AP) and 1969 (AP, UPI). Played in the American Bowl, Coaches All-American, East-West Shrine and Senior Bowl all-star games. Taken in the third round by the Baltimore Colts in the 1970 NFL draft. Field goal as clock expired boosted Baltimore to a win over Dallas in the 1971 Super Bowl. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1983.

slots.name: Vicki Niemann Englehart
slots.bio: One of the early soccer stars whose records still stand. Team's leading scorer in each of her four seasons. Concluded her career owning records for points (134) and goals (54), both of which remain. Shares the mark for most goals in a game (5) and has season records for assists (17) and points (53). Helped UC compile a 47-12-3 record, which featured two Midwest Intercollegiate Women's Soccer League titles, Top 20 rankings all four years and trips to the AIAW (1982) and NCAA (1983) postseason tournaments. Earned All-American honors (third team) in 1981 and 1983 (NSCAA). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1998.

slots.name: Bill Shalosky
slots.bio: Three-year starter at left guard, during which time he earned the reputation of being one of the top downfield blockers in college football. Earned All-Mid-American Conference and All-Ohio honors in each of his three seasons as a starter. Earned team's Most Efficient Lineman Award in 1951. Also competed in track, winning the Ohio College state title in the shot put. Honorable mention All-American in 1952 (AP, UPI, NEA). Played in the East-West Shrine and the College All-Star games. Jersey number (29) retired. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1984.

slots.name: Hal Schneider
slots.bio: One of the most decorated Bearcats of the 1940s. Two-way performer at halfback on the 1942 team that posted an 8-2 record, the lone losses to Rose Bowl-bound Georgia and Tennessee, which went on to play in the Sugar Bowl. Enlisted in the Navy for World War II and his assignment stationed him at UC's College of Medicine. Continued his athletic career, participating on the basketball teams of 1943-44-45. Cage squad's third-leading scorer his sophomore and junior campaigns. Earned a pair of letters as a pitcher on the 1942 and 1943 baseball teams and was an instrumental player when football returned in 1945. Earned his medical degree at UC's College of Medicine and later served as professor there. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1995.

slots.name: Derrek Dickey
slots.bio: Three-year starter who provided leadership by performance as well as spirit. Debuted as a sophomore (freshmen were ineligible) in 1970-71 and led UC in scoring (17.9 points) and rebounding (12.1 rebounds). Repeated as rebounding leader his junior (10.9) and senior (10.0) years and was second in scoring (18.1, 15.0) in each of those seasons. Averaged a double-double 17.0 points and 11.0 rebounds for his career while helping UC to a 48-30 record. Team MVP as a sophomore. Team captain his junior and senior seasons. Selected in the second round of the 1973 NBA Draft by Golden State and played in the NBA for five seasons. Launched his broadcasting career as analyst on the UC basketball telecasts and later moved on to ESPN and the NBA. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1988.

slots.name: Bill Faul
slots.bio: Baseball pitcher and 2012 UC Athletics Hall of Fame inductee. A GoBearcats feature credits Faul with a dominant Bearcat career, including the school record 0.80 ERA he posted after appearing on the cover of the 1962 NCAA Baseball Guide. GoBearcats coverage also notes that he led the nation with 14.6 strikeouts per game in 1961 and remained visible in the Bearcat record books decades later.

slots.name: Gary Yoder
slots.bio: A junior college transfer who played a key role in UC's success during his two-season career as a Bearcat. Point guard who helped UC compile a 50-11 record, win two Metro Conference Tournament titles and make a pair of NCAA Tournament appearances. Averaged 7.3 points and led the team in assists as a junior. Team's second-leading scorer (13.6) and assists leader as a senior. Shot .881 from the foul line as a senior, the second-highest season mark in UC history. Metro Conference Player of the Year and first team all-league selection as a senior in 1977. Named to the Metro Conference All-Tournament Team in 1977. Earned honorable mention All-American honors in 1977 (Citizens Savings Foundation). Taken in the third round of the 1977 NBA draft by Milwaukee.

slots.name: Don McMillan
slots.bio: Enrolled at UC following service in the Navy during World War II, and as a freshman, quarterbacked the Bearcats to one of their greatest seasons ever, featuring a win over defending Big Ten champion Indiana and a victory over Virginia Tech in the Sun Bowl. Four-year letterwinner. Moved to defense during his sophomore season and enjoyed similar success. Also served as the team's punter. Active in campus life, elected to the Sigma Sigma and ULEX honoraries. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1995.

slots.name: Jennifer Kemp
slots.bio: First woman in UC history to earn Associated Press and UPI All-American honors. UC team Co-Captain and team MVP in 1974. Finalist at the AIAW National Championships in 1973 and 1974. Represented the USA in the 1972 Olympics and won gold in the distance freestyle relay setting a new world record with a time of 1:57.97 seconds. Won bronze medal at the 1975 Pan American games in the 100m freestyle.

slots.name: Kevin Huber
slots.bio: Punter who became one of Cincinnati football’s most decorated specialists. GoBearcats noted that Huber broke UC’s single-season punting record and led the nation in 2007 with a 46.9-yard average, earning consensus first-team All-America honors and BIG EAST Special Teams Player of the Year. He was also a returning Ray Guy Award finalist entering 2008.

slots.name: Robert Heuck
slots.bio: Prototype of the BMOC (Big Man On Campus) who was a football star, president of the senior class and yearbook editor at UC. Scored 26 touchdowns during his three-year career, 22 by rushing, which for 61 years was the UC record. Scored a record-tying eight TDs in a 1912 game vs. Transylvania. Leader in city and county political reform following his UC days. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1981.

slots.name: Danny Barrett
slots.bio: Four-year regular who concluded his career among UC's leaders in completions (352), attempts (658), completion percentage (.535), passing yards (4,407) and touchdown passes (27). Passed for 2,222 yards and 17 TDs as a senior, at that time the second-highest yardage total in UC history. Earned honorable mention All-American honors in 1982 (AP). Played 14 seasons in the Canadian Football League and later served as head coach at Saskatchewan. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2001.

slots.name: Carl Bouldin
slots.bio: Three-year letterman in basketball. Co-captain of the 1960-61 Bearcats that won the school's first national championship. Standout pitcher on the baseball team, compiling a 14-3 record and a 238 ERA as a senior. Drafted by both the Cincinnati Royals of the NBA and the Washington Senators of major league baseball. Ultimately chose to pursue a career in pro baseball and played in the Washington and Chicago White Sox organizations. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1982.

slots.name: Chase Davies
slots.bio: A loyal advocate for Bearcat athletics, first as an undergraduate and graduate student and then from his position in the community. Earned three degrees from UC. Member of the Sigma Sigma honorary. One of the early organizers of groups to back UC's athletic program. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1980.

slots.name: John Bedway
slots.bio: Distinguished offensive lineman on the UC teams of the early 1940s, earning three letters.
